title: Integral density on curve character varieties
gap_note: The Lean states a single internal compatibility lemma of the band-cutting construction: for a proper surface diagram D (positive ranks, every seam has >=2 children) with finitely many vertices, a seam q whose parent has maximal rank and positive genus, puncture units P, a FIELD-valued solution x, and a chosen boundary occurrence (b0,i0), the 'produced marked values' satisfy the framed-flag equation at every seam s of the 'produced marked diagram' C: SameFramedFlag (C.seamGrade s) (matrixUnitEquiv (seamLeft s evaluated at v)) (matrixUnitEquiv (seamRight s evaluated at v)). Nothing in the statement mentions curves, character varieties M_r(X), SL_r, integral points over O_L, number fields, quasi-unipotent classes, Zariski density or even the paper's intermediate Diagram density theorem (diagrams.tex thm:diagram-density); R is an arbitrary commutative ring with R->K, K an arbitrary field, punctures are arbitrary units. It is a step in assembling a solution of the cut (marked) diagram (the solution module then uses it in producedMarkedSolution), i.e. the paper's rank-reduction by cutting bands (reduction.tex prop:nonclosed-reduction). The scope note (docs/027.md) says the same: existence of integral points and Zariski density are not established.
suspicious_defs: OAI/AlgebraicGeometry/CharacterVarieties/Frames/MarkedFrames.lean:16-24 `opaque cutGeneratorWitness : IdentifiedBand ... := identifiedBand ...` in the import cone: an opaque constant whose value is hidden from the kernel; the produced diagram's shape/rowRanks/colRanks (ProducedDiagram.lean:36-42) are fields of it, so the theorem is effectively about an arbitrary witness. Harmless for truth of the lemma but the 'produced' objects are not computable from the statement.

Seams/ProducedDiagram.lean:26-59 producedCutSeed/J/T/Band/MarkedDiagram/MarkedFrames/MarkedValues: the objects the lemma is about are defined through ~10 chained constructions (band-cut gauge lift, refinedMarkedDiagram, refinedMarkedLiftValues, namedCutPortFrames); nothing short of reading them tells what C and v are.

Foundation/SurfacePresentation.lean:13-24 Diagram and Foundation/Incidence.lean:253-345 VertexAssembly/PortAssembly: the paper's surface diagram encoded as occurrence/port bijections (attach : LocalPort V kind ≃ S × Bool), boundary cycles as equivalences; F,S,V : Type (universe 0), only [Finite V] assumed (S is then finite via attach; F may have extra closed facets).
SurfacePresentation.lean:62-64 Punctures: arbitrary units R^x, quasi-unipotence deliberately not imposed (docstring says imposed at density stage).

The challenge file and the Produced*/SurfacePresentation/MarkedFrames files use `open scoped Classical` (classical decidability instances) and `noncomputable section`; `Classical.choice` is within the permitted axioms.

Foundation/BoundaryCycles.lean:251-254 Proper = positive ranks and >=2 children per seam; hmax says seam q's parent has maximal rank: the proof-engineering normalisation of the paper's 'normalized diagram', not a restriction on curves.

title: Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions
gap_note: The Lean states one local-algebra/topology lemma: on a closed etale chart (A a local Noetherian domain, formally etale over k[x_sigma], essentially of finite type and formally unramified over R = k[x_sigma] localised at the origin, k algebraically closed, no characteristic hypothesis) the monomial 'retraction' valuations v_w, w in ℝ_{>=0}^sigma with sum a_i w_i = 1 (all a_i>0), extended to K = Frac A with values in ℝ ∪ {∞}, form a compact set in the pointwise topology of K -> WithTop ℝ. The solution proves it as: weights-to-valuations is continuous (continuous_closedChartFieldRetraction_evaluations) and the normalised simplex is compact. Nothing about Fano contractions, klt/lc/epsilon-lc, log discrepancies, complements, indices, Cartier divisors or lc thresholds appears. It is the compactness ingredient of the paper's Section E (lem:E-compactness: the lc slice is a compact complex of monomial valuations with continuous evaluations), which feeds the Uniform Cartier sections theorem and, via Chen's equivalence, bounded klt complements; neither that theorem (uniform Cartier sections, thm:main of the second paper) nor Theorem 1.1 / Corollary 1.2 of the Bounded klt complements paper is stated. Matches the scope note, which says the same.
suspicious_defs: CartierChartCompactnessSupport.lean:11-23 hypotheses are 14 typeclass binders (IsAlgClosed k, IsLocalization.AtPrime R (idealOfVars), IsLocalHom, FormallyUnramified R A, EssFiniteType R A, FormallyEtale (MvPolynomial sigma k) A, IsFractionRing A K, ...), all in one universe u; the encoding of 'closed etale chart' is by these classes. They are satisfiable (A = R = localisation of k[x_sigma] at the origin, K = k(x_sigma)), so the lemma is not vacuous.

CartierSections/FieldRetraction.lean:30-33 closedChartFieldRetraction and ChartRetraction.lean:37-56: valuation = monomial valuation of the Taylor expansion A -> k[[x_sigma]] obtained from the completion isomorphism (closedChartEquiv, built from polynomialChartSeriesEquiv + completionIdealCongr); weights may be 0 (boundary faces), values in ENNReal on A and WithTop ℝ on K; extended to the fraction field by fractionValuation (FractionValuation.lean:66-70, via extendToLocalization).

CartierChartCompactnessSupport.lean:11-13 `local instance polynomialOrigin_isMaximal_topology` re-exports the proved theorem polynomialOrigin_isMaximal (ClosedCharts.lean:71-75) as an instance: no axiom involved.
Topology: product topology on K -> WithTop ℝ, WithTop ℝ carrying the order topology (Mathlib/Topology/Order/WithTop.lean:26); 'pointwise topology on the fraction field', as the scope note says.

title: The $L\log L$ Fourier-convergence conjecture
gap_note: The Lean theorem OAI.FourierLLogL.paperMain is the paper's Theorem 1.1 verbatim: for f on AddCircle (2*pi) with AEStronglyMeasurable and Integrable (||f|| * log(2+||f||)) w.r.t. the normalised Haar measure, there is a measurable null set E with S_N f x -> f x for x outside E along N : Nat. Only unpacking is needed: haarAddCircle is dx/(2pi), fourierCoeff/fourier are fhat(k) and e^{ikx}, and the Integrable hypothesis is the paper's definition of L log L (f is automatically in L^1, so fourierCoeff is the genuine integral).
suspicious_defs: AddCircle (2 * Real.pi): standard Mathlib quotient R/(2 pi Z); the paper's T
AddCircle.haarAddCircle: standard Mathlib Haar measure normalised to total mass 1 (addHaarMeasure top, IsProbabilityMeasure), equal to dx/(2 pi) for period 2 pi; matches the paper's mu; standard

fourierCoeff: standard Mathlib n-th coefficient = integral of fourier (-n) t * f t d(haarAddCircle) = integral of f(x) e^{-inx} dx/(2 pi); Bochner integral so junk value 0 for non-integrable f, but the hypotheses force f in L^1 (||f|| log 2 <= ||f|| log(2+||f||)); standard
fourier k x: standard Mathlib exponential monomial toCircle(k . x) = exp(2 pi i k x / T) = e^{ikx} for T = 2 pi; standard
Finset.Icc (-(N:Z)) (N:Z) with Filter.atTop on N : Nat: the symmetric partial sum over |k| <= N along the full sequence; standard
Integrable (fun x => ||f x|| * Real.log (2 + ||f x||)) haarAddCircle: exactly the paper's L log L(T) class (introduction.tex:11-15); standard
circlePeriod_pos: local instance Fact (0 < 2*Real.pi) (proved by mul_pos and Real.pi_pos); needed for haarAddCircle/fourier, adds no hypothesis

title: Derandomization of logarithmic space: $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$
gap_note: Lean states `L = RL ∧ RL = BPL` for binary languages in an explicit multi-head, multi-tape logspace Turing-machine model (one fresh coin per step, polynomial clock on every coin tape, RL = 0 / >= 1/2, BPL = <= 1/3 / >= 2/3), which is the paper's Theorem (introduction.tex:28-32) after unfolding L, RL, BPL and chaining the two equalities; the binary-alphabet convention is the only routine step. The summary's second sentence (effective compiler with explicit polynomial running-time bounds, compiler.tex:8-19) has no Lean statement, as the scope note says.
suspicious_defs: Word / Language: languages are sets of binary words (List Bool) only; the paper does not fix the alphabet in its Section 1, so the reduction from larger alphabets is a routine encoding step, not a restriction on the class.

Machine / Action / Configuration: finite transition-table machine with q+1 states, w two-way-infinite binary work tapes (blank = false) and h read-only two-way input heads, with q, w, h chosen existentially; standard, and matches the paper's 'finite control, endmarked read-only input, finitely many work tapes' model (introduction.tex:10-15).

Machine.step / run: one fresh coin bit per step (coins t used at step t+1), halting states are fixed points; matches 'fresh independent fair bits' and cannot reuse a past coin except via finite control.

Machine.LogSpace: space = number of distinct cells visited by each work head up to time t, summed over tapes, bounded by c * Nat.clog 2 (|x|+2) for every input, every coin tape and every time t; standard counted-cell convention (blank-cell visits count), same as the paper.

Machine.Decides: for every x some time t with all coin tapes halted with output b and (b = true <-> x in A); no explicit time bound is imposed on L-machines (polynomial time follows from the configuration count, as the paper notes at introduction.tex:20-22); standard.
Machine.HaltsBy: halting by the clock on EVERY coin tape (worst-case time), as the paper requires ('All randomized running-time bounds hold on every random tape'); standard.
Machine.acceptanceProbability: exact fraction of the 2^t coin strings of length t (padded with false) whose time-t state outputs true, with t = polynomialClock c k |x| = c*(|x|+2)^k; standard.
RL / BPL: thresholds are exactly 0 on no and >= 1/2 on yes (RL), <= 1/3 on no and >= 2/3 on yes (BPL), as in introduction.tex:22-26; standard.

title: One-tape time simulation in two-fifths-power space
gap_note: Lean `capped` and `unknown` are the two clauses of the paper's single main theorem (introduction.tex:64-79) with `Single` = the fixed one-writable-tape machine, `Access` = the polylog-space accessor condition, `outcome` = (finite-control state, halted flag) with absorbing halting states, `Within` = work-space bits with no time bound, and `c*T^(2/5)*(log2(T+2))^e` = O~(T^{2/5}); no step beyond unfolding these definitions is needed. The summary's remark 'improving the square-root exponent' is a comparison with the classical bound, not a separate formal claim.
suspicious_defs: Single.sensor: initial writable-tape contents (tag none) and the symbols read by each of the `heads` read-only heads (tag some i) are an arbitrary function List X -> Option (Fin heads) -> Z -> A, constrained only through the `Access` hypothesis; input symbols share the tape alphabet A. This is the paper's 'uniform interface' (introduction.tex:33-38), not a restriction. The tape contents sensor x none do not depend on T by construction.

Single.Access: the polylog-space accessor hypothesis is part of the statement (the theorem is conditional on it, per pair (x,T), as in the paper): a fixed uniform TM A, given x, the cap T, the tag, and the sign and magnitude of l in binary, outputs sensor x h l within p*(log2(T+2))^q work bits for every tag and every |l| <= T. In `unknown` it is required for every T >= 2.

TM / TM.Within / Window.bits: simulator and accessor model is a multi-tape machine (finite Q, finitely many work tapes with finite alphabets) with endmarked read-only heads on the public word and on each binary argument tape; space = sum over work tapes of (window span including the origin) * bit-width of the alphabet; input and cap tapes are not charged; NO time bound (matches 'simulation time is unrestricted'); standard counted-cell convention.

Single.move / Single.outcome: halted states are absorbing (state, tape symbol and head positions unchanged), and outcome x n = (state, halted flag) after exactly n steps, so it equals the 'finite-control and halting outcome by time n'.
[Fintype X]: the public alphabet is finite.

Cost.Log / Cost.exponent: Log T = Real.log (T+2) / Real.log 2 (binary log of T+2); exponent = 2/5 used as a real power; the log exponent e is a natural number and c a positive real, both existentially quantified before x and T (they may depend on M, A, p, q only), matching O~ with 'a fixed constant C'.
Mark.see / Mark.walk: read-only inputs are endmarked (0 = left marker, 1..len = symbols, len+1 = right marker) and heads are confined to [0, len+1]; standard.

title: A counterexample to the small Cohen--Macaulay module conjecture
gap_note: The Lean theorem is only an existence statement for a C-algebra R that is a Noetherian, integrally closed, local, I-adically complete domain with ringKrullDim R = 3 and C -> residue field bijective. It never mentions modules, depth or Cohen-Macaulayness, so the defining property of the counterexample (no nonzero finitely generated module of depth 3) is absent and no routine step supplies it. As written the statement is satisfied by C[[x,y,z]] (regular local, whose free module R is maximal CM), and the witness is not tied to the Kummer-surface cone. It is the ring-structure lemma on the candidate (paper Sec. 2: complete, normal, dim 3, residue field C) used inside the proof of Thm 1.1, not the headline. The lab's scope note agrees: 'verifies only the ring-theoretic candidate ... does not assert the absence of small Cohen-Macaulay modules'. The summary's second sentence (the localization T_n essentially of finite type over C, Cor. 7.1 = cor:affine-local, paper.tex:646-) has no challenge statement either.

title: Classification by trace cones after Razak--Jacelon stabilization
gap_note: The Lean file never mentions the Razak–Jacelon algebra, K, tensor products, separability, nuclearity or any *-isomorphism. It defines the trace cone of a general C*-algebra (ExtendedTrace, CanonicalConvergence, TraceConeEquiv, ClosedIdeal) and proves, via 17 sorry'd lemmas, that a trace-cone equivalence F induces an order isomorphism of closed ideals with F(finIdeal τ) = finIdeal(F τ) and F(zeroIdeal τ) = zeroIdeal(F τ), together with the ideal-weight facts it needs (weight τ_I exists, additive idempotents = ideal weights, I ≤ J iff τ_I + τ_J = τ_I, closure/ideal/lsc properties of the finite domain). This is a necessary-consequence lemma of a cone isomorphism: part of the paper's Sec. 2 Proposition 'Transport of ideals' (not its Cuntz-semigroup or primitive-space clauses). Nothing builds an algebra isomorphism; stabilization models, norm uniqueness and intertwining (paper Sec. 3-8) are absent, so no routine step reaches Thm 1.1. Agrees with the lab's scope note ('supporting ideal-transport result', 'does not establish that conclusion').
suspicious_defs: TraceIdealTransportSupport.lean:10 C*-algebra encoded as [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]: the order is a separate instance, pinned to the usual C*-order by StarOrderedRing (x ≤ y iff y - x is a sum of s*s). Standard Mathlib idiom; Positive A := {a // 0 ≤ a} (:12) has the subtype norm topology.

TraceIdealTransportSupport.lean:27-34 ExtendedTrace: ℝ≥0∞-valued, additive, homogeneous for r>0, τ(x*x)=τ(xx*), LowerSemicontinuous in the norm topology; no density condition on the finite domain. Matches the paper's T(C).

TraceIdealTransportSupport.lean:22-24,39-43 canonical topology is not defined as a topology: CanonicalConvergence says limsup τ_i((a-ε)_+) ≤ σ(a) ≤ liminf τ_i(a) along an arbitrary filter l, (a-ε)_+ via cfcₙ; :206-218 TraceConeEquiv requires bijection + additivity, zero, scaling (r>0) and preservation of this convergence in both directions (a homeomorphism only if the convergence is topological, an unproved background fact from Elliott–Robert–Santiago).

TraceIdealTransportSupport.lean:70,90 finiteIdeal := topological closure of {x | τ(x*x) < ∞}; paper's Fin(τ) is the closed ideal generated by finite-trace positives (equal, routine). :137-149 zeroIdeal := finIdeal of supportWeight (paper's Ker(τ)). :155-156 ClosedIdeal.weight := Classical.choose of closed_ideal_weight_exists (determined, since τ a = if a ∈ I then 0 else ∞). Sorried lemmas feed only proof fields (finiteSquareAlgebra, finIdeal, supportWeight) and, for weight, a Classical.choose of an existence theorem with a unique witness, so no definition carries a junk value.
TraceIdealTransportSupport.lean:6 'open ... Classical' (classical Decidable instances for the ifs); the config enables nanoda for this challenge.
